-- Give each Content attached to Document 21212 (megacoglab, NULL source_local_id)
-- its own Document, the way upsert_content does today (content_as_document = true):
-- one Document per Content source_local_id, same id, created/last_modified/author from the Content.
-- Then delete Document 21212, which nothing points at any more.
-- Ends without COMMIT: check the SELECT results, then run COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

BEGIN;

-- 1. One Document per distinct Content source_local_id. Skip ids that already have a Document.
INSERT INTO public."Document" (space_id, source_local_id, created, last_modified, author_id, content_type)
SELECT
    c.space_id,
    c.source_local_id,
    min(c.created),
    max(c.last_modified),
    coalesce(
        (array_agg(c.author_id ORDER BY c.id) FILTER (WHERE c.author_id IS NOT NULL))[1],
        d.author_id
    ),
    CASE s.platform::text
        WHEN 'Roam' THEN 'text/roam+markdown'
        WHEN 'Obsidian' THEN 'text/obsidian+markdown'
        ELSE 'text/plain' END
FROM public."Content" AS c
JOIN public."Document" AS d ON d.id = c.document_id
JOIN public."Space" AS s ON s.id = c.space_id
WHERE c.document_id = 21212
GROUP BY c.space_id, c.source_local_id, d.author_id, s.platform
ON CONFLICT (space_id, source_local_id) DO NOTHING;

-- 2. Point each Content at the Document with its own source_local_id.
UPDATE public."Content" AS c
SET document_id = nd.id
FROM public."Document" AS nd
WHERE c.document_id = 21212
  AND nd.space_id = c.space_id
  AND nd.source_local_id = c.source_local_id;

-- 3. Checks. Expect 0, then 0.
SELECT count(*) AS still_on_21212 FROM public."Content" WHERE document_id = 21212;
SELECT count(*) AS null_id_documents FROM public."Document" WHERE source_local_id IS NULL AND id <> 21212;

-- 4. Remove the orphan. Cascades nothing once step 3 shows 0.
DELETE FROM public."Document" WHERE id = 21212;

-- COMMIT;   -- or ROLLBACK;

content.text:
Don't delete Document 21212. That would cascade-delete its 72 Content rows. I wrote a repair script that gives each of those Content rows its own Document, which is what sync would build today.

**Why 72 rows are still on it:** current sync calls `upsert_concepts` with `content_as_document = true`. That gives every Content its own Document with the same `source_local_id`. The upsert's conflict clause also replaces `document_id` with the new Document. So whenever megacoglab re-sent one of those nodes, it moved off 21212. The 72 still attached are nodes that haven't been re-sent since May 2025. Either they haven't changed since, or they're gone from the graph. That's also why they have different ids: each is a separate node that the early sync code put in one shared Document.

**The repair** is at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maparent-OpenSource-discourse-graph/4f74a5b0-e4f9-4990-8212-b5c1f88251d8/scratchpad/repair_document_21212.sql`. Inside one transaction it:
1. Creates one Document for each distinct Content `source_local_id`. It uses the Content's earliest `created`, latest `last_modified` and author. If no Content has an author, it falls back to 21212's author. The content type comes from the space's platform. Ids that already have a Document are skipped.
2. Points each Content at the Document with its own id.
3. Prints two counts, both of which should be 0: Content still on 21212, and other Documents with a NULL id.
4. Deletes 21212.

The script ends without `COMMIT`, so you can check the counts and then commit or roll back. I checked the column names against the schema but haven't run the script anywhere.

If some of those 72 nodes no longer exist in Roam, their Content stays as stale rows. It would be the same if sync had moved them. That's the missing-delete-cascades problem, not this ticket's.

Once production has no NULL-id Documents, the first Done When item can simply say that ENG-2452, your deletion of Document 21177 and this repair cleared all three tables. I'll also drop the `upsert_content` error-reporting line. Should I apply the generalized redraft to ENG-2489 with those two changes?

Agreed, I'll stop there. What I verified:

- **Timing:** both Documents were created right after their spaces, on May 16 and May 22, 2025. They're 1 and 3 ids after the space on the shared `entity_id_seq`.
- **Old code:** the full sync code landed in June 2025, after both. On May 13, 2025, a pre-merge branch had `apps/roam/src/utils/embeddingWorkflow.ts` fetching or creating a Document while inserting nodes.

What I assumed but didn't read: that this branch created one Document per graph with no id and attached every node's Content to it. That would explain 72 different ids sharing one Document.

Current code can't do this. `upsert_content` creates a Document only when it has a `source_local_id`, and by default it uses the Content's own id. So the repair script still fits, and the NOT NULL ticket closes the door for good.

input.title: Make `source_local_id` NOT NULL on Concept, Content and Document
input.description:
## Problem

- Concept, Content and Document all accept a row with no `source_local_id`. Their unique indexes on `source_local_id` declare `NULLS DISTINCT`, so any number of these rows can coexist. Sync can't find or update such a row.
- On Concept, such rows also hold their name in the `(space_id, name)` index. On 2026-11-03, 708 of them stopped Roam sync in the discourse-graphs space. Nothing stops new ones in any of the three tables.
- `_local_concept_to_db_concept` still turns an empty `source_local_id` into NULL, and the schema accepts the row without an error. The bad row only shows up later, when something collides.
- The client sync code is likely to change a lot, so the protection belongs in the database.

## Solution

- Add NOT NULL to `source_local_id` on Concept, Content and Document, in the schema and in a migration.
- Recreate their unique indexes that include `source_local_id` without `NULLS DISTINCT`.

## Done When

- The migration applies on production and on a fresh local database.
- Inserting a row with a NULL or empty `source_local_id` into any of the three tables fails.
- No unique index on these tables that includes `source_local_id` declares `NULLS DISTINCT`, in the schema or the migration.
- In `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`, a row with a missing or empty `source_local_id` returns an error value with a warning that names the column, and the other rows in the batch are still saved. Tests cover this.
- The existing database test suite passes.

## Out of Scope

- How a future web-created node gets its `source_local_id`. Web nodes will need one, but the id scheme isn't decided.
- Client-side handling of error results in Roam or Obsidian sync.

## Notes

- As of 2026-11-13, production has no NULL `source_local_id` in the three tables. ENG-2452 deleted the 708 Concepts. Two Documents remained, both created in May 2025 by pre-release code. Document 21177 (discourse-dev-graph) had no Content and was deleted. Document 21212 (megacoglab) held 72 Content rows; each now has its own Document with its `source_local_id`, as current sync builds them, and 21212 was deleted.
- All Concept fixtures in the cucumber features already set `source_local_id`. Content and Document fixtures need the same check.
- `upsert_content` is expected to give way to `upsert_concepts` with embedded Content, but that move isn't scheduled.
- Source: Roam issue candidate `0nLVRPvPo`.
- Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

{"id":"ENG-2489","uuid":"fce7af7c-d7b1-4fc1-bf07-2270a96e5ffd","title":"Make `source_local_id` NOT NULL on Concept, Content and Document","description":"## Problem

* Concept, Content and Document all accept a row with no `source_local_id`. Their unique indexes on `source_local_id` declare `NULLS DISTINCT`, so any number of these rows can coexist. Sync can't find or update such a row.
* On Concept, such rows also hold their name in the `(space_id, name)` index. On 2026-11-03, 708 of them stopped Roam sync in the discourse-graphs space. Nothing stops new ones in any of the three tables.
* `_local_concept_to_db_concept` still turns an empty `source_local_id` into NULL, and the schema accepts the row without an error. The bad row only shows up later, when something collides.
* The client sync code is likely to change a lot, so the protection belongs in the database.

## Solution

* Add NOT NULL to `source_local_id` on Concept, Content and Document, in the schema and in a migration.
* Recreate their unique indexes that include `source_local_id` without `NULLS DISTINCT`.

## Done When

* The migration applies on production and on a fresh local database.
* Inserting a row with a NULL or empty `source_local_id` into any of the three tables fails.
* No unique index on these tables that includes `source_local_id` declares `NULLS DISTINCT`, in the schema or the migration.
* In `upsert_concepts` and `upsert_content`, a row with a missing or empty `source_local_id` returns an error value with a warning that names the column, and the other rows in the batch are still saved. Tests cover this.
* The existing database test suite passes.

## Out of Scope

* How a future web-created node gets its `source_local_id`. Web nodes will need one, but the id scheme isn't decided.
* Client-side handling of error results in Roam or Obsidian sync.

## Notes

* As of 2026-11-13, production has no NULL `source_local_id` in the three tables. <issue id="254439d3-63e1-4619-b8b0-d4f375c800a7" label="ENG-2452" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2452/delete-concept-rows-with-no-source-local-id-from-the-discourse-graphs" /> deleted the 708 Concepts. Two Documents remained, both created in May 2025 by pre-release code. Document 21177 (discourse-dev-graph) had no Content and was deleted. Document 21212 (megacoglab) held 72 Content rows; each now has its own Document with its `source_local_id`, as current sync builds them, and 21212 was deleted.
* All Concept fixtures in the cucumber features already set `source_local_id`. Content and Document fixtures need the same check.
* `upsert_content` is expected to give way to `upsert_concepts` with embedded Content, but that move isn't scheduled.
* Source: Roam issue candidate `0nLVRPvPo`.

---
name: null-local-id-concepts
description: Roam sync failure on discourse-graphs from 708 legacy Concept rows with NULL source_local_id holding their names; state as of 2026-11-03
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: efd9bd90-060c-4e7f-be24-5070fdbccc58
  modified: 2026-11-13T19:19:54.491Z
---

Production space 161470 (discourse-graphs) has 708 of 1432 Concepts with NULL source_local_id: all node instances, no dependents via schema_id or refs, 0 concept_contributors, no other space affected. All 20 names logged with `-1` by upsert_concepts on 2026-11-03 are among them. Export at repo root: missing_local_id.csv.

Likely origin, inferred from code and ids, no log of the run: the ids are contiguous (161540 to 162247), only 69 ids after the space id on the shared entity_id_seq. In October 2025 an embedding failure returned without throwing, so concepts were upserted with no Content, and the Content lookup left represented_by_id NULL. The earlier "Content rows were deleted via ON DELETE SET NULL" account was wrong; I told the user so.

The three `-2` rows look like knock-ons: a failed Source leaves its citing node's reference NULL, jsonb_set returns NULL, and reference_content breaks NOT NULL.

ENG-2452 (Ticket Draft, human review pending) covers the delete. The NOT NULL issue candidate is at Roam 0nLVRPvPo, on the 2026-11-03 daily note, and may get moved. They link to each other. Delete not yet run, as of 2026-11-03. epistemic_status and description check on the 708 rows still unanswered.

On 2026-11-05 the user first withdrew NOT NULL for pure-web Concepts, then reinstated it the same day, accepting that web nodes will need a `source_local_id`. Expected model, not built: web nodes live in Concept and Content, in a Space with a new platform type ("DGWeb or some such"), written through upsert_concepts or similar; a published API likely exposes JSON-LD or CrossApp nodes. How the id is generated isn't settled: the user is reluctant to add an id separate from the database id, and I recommended an API-generated UUID. The user had said 0nLVRPvPo needs a serious review before acting on it, so nothing was changed there.

Update 2026-11-13: ENG-2452 is Done. The NOT NULL candidate became ENG-2489 (Ticket Draft, Engineering Ops assorted tasks), with web-node ids, Content/Document and client `-2` handling out of scope.

**Why:** the user wants the ticket to argue why this will not recur, and to leave future solutions open: a references on-delete trigger is undecided, and continuing after a failed batch must not advance last success time. Client error handling gets notes, not an issue candidate.

**How to apply:** check whether the delete has run before re-diagnosing. Related: [[tickets-state-goals-not-methods]], [[missing-delete-cascades]], [[ticket-before-code]].
